content.text:
`slugify` now works in `src/strings.js`, and `npm test` passes all 13 tests (the 2 existing ones plus 11 new).

It follows your rules in order:
- It maps `đ`/`Đ` to `d`.
- It removes diacritics.
- It lowercases.
- It turns each run of characters outside a-z and 0-9 into one hyphen.
- It trims the leading hyphen, cuts to 50 characters, then trims any trailing hyphen. Trimming after the cut is what keeps a slug cut at 50 from ending with a hyphen.

The new tests are in `test/strings.test.js`. They cover:
- Vietnamese and other Latin diacritics, plus `đ`/`Đ`.
- Hyphen collapsing and trimming.
- Digits.
- Input made only of symbols, which gives an empty string.
- The 50-character cut, including two cases where the cut lands next to a hyphen.

The function converts its input with `String(text)` first, so a non-string argument is converted to text instead of throwing. I didn't call the advisor tool, since the task was small and the tests verify the result.
